newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen earnings fell in latest year.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen earnings fell in latest year.

text.p: Thyssen AG, Germany's largest steelmaker, said Friday its net profit fell to 350 million marks ($233 million) in fiscal 1996 from 775 million marks ($516 million) in 1995, and announced a major restructuring.
The company, which also makes elevators, auto components and has other holdings, cut its dividend and said it had started to sharpen its focus and shed non-core businesses.
"In view of a light upward economic development, a gradually improving development of the Thyssen Group is expected," the company said in a statement.
Pretax profits fell 36 percent as sales slipped to 38.7 billion marks ($25.8 billion) from 39.1 billion marks $26.0 billion).
"The profit figure was a bit of a shock to the system, but the real question is what are the benefits and costs of the restructuring," said analyst Glen Liddy at Kleinwort Benson in London.
Thyssen said it would reorganize its industrial portfolio into five primary and five secondary profit centres, and divest itself of money-losing and non-core operations.
The core divisions will be elevator manufacturing, automotive components, flat steel production, production systems, and materials trading.
The "potential core business areas" were construction technology, real estate, industrial services, logistics and telecommunications.
